answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because knoll only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, zephyr is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
